meta.titre: Vitamins and Mineral Salts: Functions, Sources and Deficiency Diseases
meta.sous_theme: Functions, sources and deficiency of protective nutrients
tags: vitamins and mineral salts in food

source.epreuve_titre: GCE O/L Food and Nutrition past paper (Cameroon)

sections.contenu_markdown: At a market in Buea, a mother buys oranges, tomatoes, beans and a little dried fish for her family each week. She does not know the names of the nutrients, but the fruit protects her children's gums, the beans and fish supply iron and calcium, and the red palm oil in the soup helps their eyes. Examiners know that most deficiency diseases are caused by a poor diet, so every year Paper 1 asks for the functions of vitamins and minerals and Paper 2 asks for numbered lists such as sources, signs or ways of keeping nutrients in food.

items: Nutrients are the useful substances in food: carbohydrates, fats, proteins, vitamins, mineral salts and water.
A balanced diet contains all the nutrients in the right amounts.
A deficiency disease is caused by a long shortage of one nutrient in the diet.

sections.titre: Functions, sources and deficiency of vitamins and minerals
sections.contenu_markdown:
### What they are
Vitamins and mineral salts are **protective nutrients**. The body needs them in small amounts. They do not give energy, but they help the body use other nutrients and stay healthy. A long shortage causes a **deficiency disease**. Vitamins A, D and K are fat-soluble (found with fats and oils); vitamin B group and vitamin C are water-soluble.

### Vitamins: function, sources, deficiency

| Vitamin | Main functions | Good sources | Deficiency |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | healthy eyes, seeing in dim light, healthy skin | liver, egg yolk, red palm oil, carrots, dark green leaves | night blindness |
| B group (for example B1) | releases energy from food, healthy nerves | whole grains, beans, meat | beri-beri (lack of B1) |
| C | healthy gums and skin, healing of wounds, helps the body absorb iron | oranges, guavas, tomatoes, fresh green peppers | scurvy |
| D | helps the body absorb calcium and phosphorus for bones and teeth | oily fish, egg yolk, margarine; also made in the skin by sunlight | rickets |
| K | helps blood to clot | green leafy vegetables | slow clotting, bleeding |

### Mineral salts: function, sources, deficiency

| Mineral | Main functions | Good sources | Deficiency |
|---|---|---|---|
| Calcium | strong bones and teeth, blood clotting, working of muscles | milk, cheese, small fish eaten whole, green leaves | weak bones and teeth |
| Iron | makes haemoglobin in red blood cells, which carries oxygen | liver, red meat, beans, dark green leaves | anaemia |
| Iodine | used to make thyroxine in the thyroid gland | sea fish, iodised salt | goitre |
| Fluoride | hardens tooth enamel | some water supplies | tooth decay |

So **blood clotting** needs vitamin K and calcium.

variantes.nom: Factors that reduce vitamin C in food
variantes.quand_utiliser: When asked for the factors that affect, reduce or destroy a vitamin in food.

variantes.nom: How to answer a numbered-list question
variantes.quand_utiliser: When the question says state, list, outline or give a number of points.
variantes.contenu_markdown: Command words such as **state**, **name** and **list** want short points; **outline** wants the main points in a few words each; **explain** wants a reason after each point. Write exactly the number asked, as a numbered list, and make each point different (heat and boiling count as one idea, so give heat once and then a different idea such as water or air). One clear point is worth one mark, so do not pad.

sections.enonce_markdown: (a) Name the deficiency disease caused by a lack of iron. (b) State two signs of this disease. (c) Give three foods that help to prevent it. (d) Name one vitamin that helps the body to absorb iron. (7 marks)

etapes.action: Read the command words and count the marks.
etapes.justification: Part (a) wants a name, (b) two signs, (c) three foods, (d) one vitamin. That is 1 + 2 + 3 + 1 = 7 points, one mark each, and no explanation is needed.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Four short answers, written in the exact numbers asked.

etapes.justification: Iron is used to make haemoglobin, which carries oxygen in red blood cells. With too little iron, too little oxygen reaches the body.

etapes.action: Choose the signs from the effect of too little oxygen.
etapes.justification: Less oxygen means less energy for the body, and fewer red cells makes the skin look pale.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Signs: tiredness and a pale skin (breathlessness and weakness are also accepted).

etapes.action: Choose foods that are rich in iron, and a vitamin linked to its absorption.
etapes.justification: Liver, red meat, beans and dark green leaves all contain iron. Vitamin C helps the body to absorb iron from food.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Foods: liver, beans, dark green leaves. Vitamin: vitamin C.

sections.conclusion_markdown: (a) Anaemia. (b) 1. Tiredness. 2. Pale skin. (c) 1. Liver. 2. Beans. 3. Dark green leaves. (d) Vitamin C. Seven short answers give the seven marks: the number of points written matches the number asked.

items.erreur_markdown: Writing that a lack of vitamin C causes rickets.
items.pourquoi_faux: Rickets is the bone disease linked to vitamin D (and calcium). The disease caused by too little vitamin C is scurvy, with bleeding gums and slow healing of wounds.
items.correction_markdown: Vitamin C: scurvy. Vitamin D: rickets. Learn each vitamin with its one disease.

items.erreur_markdown: Saying that calcium or vitamins give the body energy.
items.pourquoi_faux: Only carbohydrates, fats and (when needed) proteins supply energy. Vitamins and minerals are protective nutrients; vitamin B group only helps to release the energy that is already in food.
items.correction_markdown: Write that calcium builds bones and teeth and helps blood to clot; vitamin B helps to release energy from food.

items.erreur_markdown: Giving the five factors that affect vitamin C as: cooking, boiling, heating, overcooking, using fire.
items.pourquoi_faux: All five are the same idea (heat). The examiner gives one mark for that idea, so the answer scores about 1 out of 5.
items.correction_markdown: Give five different ideas: long cooking time, large amount of water, chopping small, adding bicarbonate of soda, long storage.

items.erreur_markdown: Naming carrots as the main source of vitamin C and oranges as the main source of vitamin A.
items.pourquoi_faux: The two are swapped. Oranges and guavas are classic sources of vitamin C; carrots, red palm oil and liver are classic sources of vitamin A.
items.correction_markdown: Vitamin C: oranges, guavas, tomatoes. Vitamin A: carrots, red palm oil, liver, egg yolk.

items.enonce_markdown: Match each nutrient (a) iodine, (b) vitamin D, (c) iron, (d) vitamin A with its function: **1** needed to make haemoglobin; **2** helps the body absorb calcium; **3** helps a person see in dim light; **4** needed to make thyroxine.
items.solution_markdown: Iodine is used to make thyroxine, vitamin D helps the absorption of calcium, iron is part of haemoglobin, and vitamin A helps vision in dim light. Answer: **(a) 4, (b) 2, (c) 1, (d) 3**. (Award a mark for each correct pair.)

items.enonce_markdown: Ngum chops cabbage into very small pieces, boils it in a large pot of water for 40 minutes without a lid, adds bicarbonate of soda to keep it green, and pours the water away. (a) Name the vitamin that is mainly lost. (b) State four faults in her method. (c) Describe how to cook the cabbage better.
items.solution_markdown: (a) **Vitamin C** (some B vitamins are also lost, because they dissolve in water). (b) Any four of: pieces too small, so more surface meets air and water; too much water; cooking time too long; no lid, so air gets in; bicarbonate of soda, an alkali, destroys vitamin C; the water that holds dissolved vitamins is thrown away. (c) Cut in larger pieces, boil in a small amount of water with a lid for a short time, add no bicarbonate, serve at once and keep the cooking water for soup. (Award a mark per correct fault, up to 4.)

items.enonce_markdown: A three-year-old child is fed mainly on cassava paste and a thin soup, with almost no milk, fish or eggs, and is kept indoors most of the day. The child's legs are bowed. (a) Name the condition. (b) Name the two nutrients whose lack is the cause. (c) Explain why the bones become soft. (d) Suggest three changes to improve the child's care.
items.solution_markdown: (a) **Rickets**. (b) **Vitamin D and calcium**. (c) Bones are hardened by calcium and phosphorus. Without vitamin D the body cannot absorb calcium properly, so the bones stay soft and bend under the weight of the child. (d) Give milk, small fish eaten whole, egg yolk or other foods rich in calcium and vitamin D; let the child play outdoors in sunlight, because the skin makes vitamin D in sunlight; give a balanced diet instead of cassava alone.

items_markdown: Vitamins and mineral salts are protective nutrients: they give no energy but keep the body healthy.
Learn each vitamin with its function, source and disease: A (night blindness), B1 (beri-beri), C (scurvy), D (rickets), K (blood clotting).
Learn each mineral the same way: calcium (bones, teeth, clotting), iron (anaemia), iodine (goitre), fluoride (teeth).
Vitamin C is lost by heat, water, air, alkali, long storage and standing, so cook vegetables quickly in a little water with a lid.
In a numbered-list question write exactly the number of points asked, each one a different idea.
